chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
There is no walimah except in five cases: at a wedding, or childbirth, or circumcision, or when acquiring a house, or upon returning from Makkah.
So al-ʿurs means marriage, al-khurs means postnatal childbirth, al-ʿidhār means circumcision, al-wikār means a man buying a house, and al-rikāz means a man returning from Makkah.

key_terms.خُرْسٍ: Childbirth, explained here as postnatal occasion with a child.
key_terms.وَلِيمَةَ: A feast or banquet held on a recognized occasion.
key_terms.وِكَارٍ: A man acquiring or buying a house.

ai.seo_question: On which occasions is a walimah held according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies five occasions on which a walimah is held: marriage, childbirth, circumcision, acquiring a house, and returning from Makkah. It defines each term directly and indicates recognized social occasions for hosting a communal feast.
